newsitem.title: RUSSIA: OLYMPICS-GLUM RUSSIANS PIN HOPES ON FUTURE GAMES BID.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-GLUM RUSSIANS PIN HOPES ON FUTURE GAMES BID.

text.p: Russian sports officials reacted with disappointment at St. Petersburg's failure to make the shortlist to host the 2004 Olympics on Friday but hoped for better luck next time -- or even later.

"It's definitely not the most brilliant day for our whole team. But we are keeping our spirits up -- we still have 2008 and 2012," said a senior official at the St Petersburg bidding committee, who asked not to be identified.

"It's sad news for us," said Gennady Alyoshin, first vice president of the Russian Olympic Committee in Moscow after the International Olympic Committee (IOC) announced in Lausanne that St. Petersburg was among the six of the 11 candidates eliminated.
"We thought and still believe St. Petersburg is a good venue for any competition including the Olympics. We will continue to hope," he said, adding that Russia may bid for the next Games.
The IOC will make a final choice for 2004 in September between Athens, Buenos Aires, Cape Town, Rome and Stockholm.

The Russian government had thrown its weight fully behind the bid, arguing that hosting the event in the city once known as Leningrad would be an international stamp of approval of its efforts to replace communism with democracy.
Kremlin officials had no immediate comment.
Russia's money troubles have left St. Petersburg in a poor state of repair and it was always an outsider in the race.
